refuted.claim: Fact 19: 'When the A-field word mark is sensed the extension latch is set and remaining commas in the B field are set to blanks; no further A-field characters are transferred. Figure 34 steps 36-37 show 0 and , positions being blanked after the A word mark at step 35.'
refuted.why: The rule is real but the cited evidence is wrong, and the 'no further A-field characters are transferred' half is wrong in a way that changes emulator output. In A22-0526-3 Figure 34 / S223-2698 Figure 23B, step 35 is the A-cycle that reads the word-marked '0' at 12156. Step 36 then STORES that A character into B position 04670 (B-field goes from $b02,574.26bbbb** to $002,574.26bbbb**) - it does not blank anything. Step 37 reads the '$' at 04669 and stores it back unchanged apart from its word mark. No comma is blanked anywhere in this trace: the comma at 04673 is read at step 43 and returned unchanged, because the significant digit '2' at step 42 had already reset the zero-suppress latch. The only blanking in the trace is at steps 40-41 (second scan), where the zeros at 04670 and 04671 are replaced with blanks.
refuted.correction: Two corrections. (1) The A character already sitting in the A-data register when the A-field word mark is sensed IS still stored into the B field on the following B-cycle; only further A-CYCLES stop. S223-2698 p.50: 'an A-field character stored in the A-data register on an A-cycle might remain in the register until the CPU executes several B-cycles'; cube1us UI1410DATA.cpp tests A_Reg->Get().TestWM() only AFTER the store, then sets SUB_SCAN_E. (2) The comma-blanking rule is a first-scan EXTENSION-subscan rule, not something visible at steps 36-37: while the extension latch is set, a comma read from the B field is replaced with a blank. cube1us first scan, extension branch: 'if (... || b_temp.TestChar(BCD_AMPERSAND) || b_temp.TestChar(BCD_COMMA)) first_scan_store_type = 2' (store a blank). simh i7010_cpu.c scan 1: 'case CHR_COM: if (cy & 0x40) WriteP(STAR, 0);' where 0x40 is the extension latch. The PoO sentence itself (A22-0526-3 p.31, 'When the A-field word mark is sensed, the remaining commas in the B-field are set to blanks') is verified; only the Figure-34 citation and the 'no further A-field characters' phrasing are wrong.
refuted.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf (A22-0526-3, p.31 and Figure 34 steps 35-43, pp.34-35); https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/S223-2698_CE_Instruction_1411_Instructions_and_Special_Features_1961.pdf (S223-2698, p.50 and Figure 23B p.53); https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp (T1410CPU::InstructionEdit, first-scan extension branch)

refuted.claim: Summary text: 'the PoO editing text says "the B-field (high-order) word mark is sensed and removed" for every variant'.
refuted.why: Not true for Sign Control Left. A22-0526-3 p.33, Sign Control Left, FORWARD SCAN step 4 reads only: 'The scan proceeds until the B-field word mark is sensed, indicating the end of the body of the control word.' There is no 'and removed'. The word 'removed'/'erased' appears in the forward-scan text of zero suppression (p.31), asterisk protection (p.32), floating dollar (p.32) and decimal control (p.33) - four variants, not five. (The finder's numbered fact 2a correctly lists only those four; only the prose summary overreaches.)
refuted.correction: The conclusion - the high-order B-field word mark is always removed - is still correct, but it rests on the mechanism, not on the PoO prose. S223-2698 p.50 states it as a hardware invariant: 'A word mark is gated to the B-field only when the low-order 0 in the control word is sensed.' cube1us encodes the same thing: every first-scan store uses AsmChannelWMNone (its own comment reads 'Point 1: Store B NO WM!') except the single store that carries FirstBFieldZero. Word-mark removal is therefore unconditional on every first-scan write-back, including in the one-scan no-suppression case that no manual traces.
refuted.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf (A22-0526-3, p.33 Sign Control Left, forward scan step 4); https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/S223-2698_CE_Instruction_1411_Instructions_and_Special_Features_1961.pdf (S223-2698, p.50); https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp

refuted.claim: Open question: 'Not checked: cube1us/1410 ... It was not needed - the CE manual plus the printed trace settle the question.'
refuted.why: The CE manual plus the printed trace do NOT settle the three-scan cases - that is exactly why the finder marked CASE 3, 4 and 5 'likely'. cube1us/1410 does settle them, and it is cheap to read: T1410CPU::InstructionEdit lives in UI1410DATA.cpp lines 374-660 and the scan modifier table is one line in UI1410CPUT.cpp.
refuted.correction: Read it. UI1410CPUT.cpp line 102: 'long scan_mod[] = { 0, -1, +1, -1 };' indexed by the scan ring (OFF/1/2/3) and applied in T1410CPU::STARScan(), which is what Cycle() feeds into B_AR on every CYCLE_B. In InstructionEdit's third-scan block (subcycle 2), every terminating path sets IRingControl = true and then FALLS THROUGH to Store(...) followed by Cycle() - so the -1 is applied on the terminating cycle. That makes BAR-after = terminating-character-address minus 1 for all three three-scan cases, confirming CASE 3, 4 and 5 in an ALD-derived implementation independent of simh.

upgraded.claim: CASE 3 (three-scan floating dollar sign): BAR after = addr(position where the '$' was stored) - 1. Was 'likely'; now confirmed in an ALD-derived simulator.
upgraded.source: https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp - third scan: 'else if(b_temp.TestChar(BCD_SPACE)) { ... else if(FloatingDollarLatch) { AssemblyChannel->Set(BCD_DOLLAR); IRingControl = true; /* Stop after $ */ } }' then unconditional Store(...) and Cycle(), with scan_mod[SCAN_3] = -1 (UI1410CPUT.cpp line 102). Matches S223-2698 p.51 'The operation ends when the $ is stored in the B-field' and rcornwell/sims i7010_cpu.c OP_E third scan (WriteP CHR_DOL; break; after DownReg(BAR)).

upgraded.claim: CASE 4 (three-scan decimal control, no significant digits): BAR after = addr(decimal point in the B field) - 1. Was 'likely'.
upgraded.source: https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp - third scan: 'else if(b_temp.TestChar(BCD_0) || (b_temp.TestChar(BCD_PERIOD) && DecimalControlLatch)) { if(ZeroSuppressLatch) { AssemblyChannel->Set(AsteriskFillLatch ? BCD_ASTERISK : BCD_SPACE); IRingControl = b_temp.TestChar(BCD_PERIOD); } else if(b_temp.TestChar(BCD_PERIOD)) { IRingControl = true; } }' followed by Store + Cycle (-1). Matches S223-2698 p.51 and A22-0526-3 p.33 'The operation stops at the decimal column.'

upgraded.claim: CASE 5 (floating dollar AND decimal control both set): BAR after = addr(first blank-or-decimal read in scan 3) - 1. Was 'likely'.
upgraded.source: https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp - the third-scan block has exactly two terminating tests, the blank/$ branch and the period branch, both reached in address order as BAR walks down, both followed by the same Store + Cycle(-1). Matches S223-2698 p.51: 'the third scan and the edit operation are complete when either a decimal or blank is read out of memory and the appropriate character is returned to the B-field.'

upgraded.claim: ANSWER 2a - the high-order B-field word mark is always removed during the first scan, INCLUDING in the single-scan no-suppression case that no manual traces. Was verified only for the four traced/described variants; now verified as a hardware invariant.
upgraded.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/S223-2698_CE_Instruction_1411_Instructions_and_Special_Features_1961.pdf (S223-2698, p.50: 'A word mark is gated to the B-field only when the low-order 0 in the control word is sensed.'); https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp (every first-scan store path uses AsmChannelWMNone unless FirstBFieldZero is true)

upgraded.claim: ANSWER 2b - the automatically set word mark at the suppression-code position is always erased, and it happens on the scan-2 terminating B-cycle in ALL cases (the CE manual's account), not on the second forward scan for floating dollar (the PoO's account). The finder called this a documentation inconsistency with identical end state; the ALD-derived timing is now pinned.

Matches S223-2698 p.51 against A22-0526-3 p.32.

upgraded.claim: SIMULATOR DEVIATION in rcornwell/sims: the single-scan test reads a byte outside the control word. Was 'likely'; both sides now read directly.
upgraded.source: https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_cpu.c - 'if ((cy & 0x1) == 0 && (ReadP(BAR) & 077) != CHR_0) break;' where BAR has already been decremented past the B-field word mark, versus https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/S223-2698_CE_Instruction_1411_Instructions_and_Special_Features_1961.pdf p.50 'If the zero suppress latch is not set when the B-field word mark is sensed, the first scan and the edit operation end (no zeros in the control word).' cube1us agrees with the manual: 'if(b_temp.TestWM()) { if(ZeroSuppressLatch) {...} else { IRingControl = True; } }' - latch only, no storage read.

upgraded.claim: The A field is not modified in storage by MCE, and 'Any sign in the units position of the data field is removed during the operation' (A22-0526-3 p.31) describes the zone being dropped from the character written into the B field. Was verified only from Figure 27's before/after print; the mechanism is now identified.
upgraded.source: https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp - in the UNITS subscan, when the B character is a blank or 0, the first scan stores with AsmChannelZonesNone + AsmChannelNumA (its comment: 'Point 4: Store A Num'), i.e. numeric only; in the BODY subscan the equivalent path stores AsmChannelZonesA + AsmChannelNumA ('Point 3: Store A Chr'), zones included. The A-cycle in InstructionEdit calls Readout() and Cycle() with no Store() at all, so the A field is never written. rcornwell/sims likewise only ever calls ReadP(AAR). Confirms A22-0526-3 Figure 27 p.31, which prints the A-field as 00257426 both before and after.

upgraded.claim: Figure 34 / Figure 23B steps 36-37 really do show the high-order word mark disappearing (I doubted this from the OCR and then measured it).
upgraded.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/S223-2698_CE_Instruction_1411_Instructions_and_Special_Features_1961.pdf (S223-2698 Figure 23B, p.53). Measured column offsets in the extracted text: the overbar line above step 36 carries marks at columns 90 and 98 of the B-FIELD AT END OF CYCLE string '$002,574.26bbbb**' - i.e. over the '$' and over the '4'. The overbar line above step 37 carries a mark at column 57 (the DATA REGISTER B column, the '$' read out with its word mark) and at column 98 only - the mark over the '$' in the B field is gone. Step 46's overbar line has no mark anywhere in the B-field column.

additions.claim: The rule the 1410 Principles of Operation omits is PRINTED EXPLICITLY in the IBM 1401 Reference Manual, and it matches the 1410 derivation exactly for both one-scan and two-scan cases. A24-1403-5, 'Editing' section, 'Address Registers After Operation': without zero suppression - I-Add. Reg. NSI, A-Add. Reg. 'A-address minus the length of the A-field', B-Add. Reg. 'B-Ln'; with zero suppression - NSI, A minus LA, B-Add. Reg. 'Location of the special control zero plus 1.' Since B - LB = addr(B-field high-order position) - 1, this is verbatim the finder's CASE 1 and CASE 2. CAVEAT: this is a 1401 statement, not a 1410 one; use it as corroboration of the 1410 derivation, never as a 1410 citation. The 1401 table covers no three-scan case.
additions.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf (A24-1403-5, Editing section, immediately after Rule 7 / Figure 59, p.43)

additions.claim: 1401-vs-1410 TRAP the finder did not flag: the 1401 Reference Manual has its OWN step-by-step editing trace, Figure 58, using the IDENTICAL example - control word $bbb,bb0.bb&CR&** and A-field 00257426 - with I/A/B address-register columns. It is 41 steps against the 1410's 46, uses 3-digit addresses (A-address 0789, B-address 0300, control word at 0284-0300, suppression code at 0291), and has NO skid-cycle row. At the first-scan terminating cycle the 1401 trace shows BAR unchanged at 0284 while the word-marked '$' is read, then step 34 re-reading 0284 as the first reverse-scan cycle; the 1410 trace at the same point shows BAR going to 04668 and a labelled 'Skid B' at step 38. Anyone quoting per-step register values for this example must check which manual they are in. (Note the 1401 manual is internally inconsistent here: its own 'B-Ln' rule requires the decrement that its Figure 58 step 33 does not show, so the trace print may be in error - do not derive 1401 behaviour from it either.)
additions.source: https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf (A24-1403-5, Figure 58 'Step-by-Step Editing Operation', p.42) versus https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf (A22-0526-3, Figure 34, pp.34-35)

additions.claim: The -1/+1/-1 scan convention is confirmed as a single hardware table in cube1us/1410, the ALD-derived cycle-level 1410 simulator: 'long scan_mod[] = { 0, -1, +1, -1 };' indexed by the four-state scan ring (SSCAN_OFF, SCAN_1, SCAN_2, SCAN_3), applied in T1410CPU::STARScan() and gated into B_AR by T1410CPU::Cycle() on every CYCLE_B. This is a third independent source for the convention, alongside S223-2698 pp.50-51 and A22-0526-3 Figure 34.

The skid B-cycle PRESERVES a word mark at the byte it touches - it is not merely 'unchanged data'. cube1us stores the skid character with AsmChannelWMB (word mark taken from the B channel, i.e. regenerated) at both the scan1-to-scan2 and scan2-to-scan3 boundaries, in contrast to every other MCE store, which uses AsmChannelWMNone. An emulator that routes the skid through its normal MCE write path will silently erase a word mark belonging to the neighbouring field.

Two further rcornwell/sims deviations the finder did not list, beyond the single-scan test. (1) The scan2-to-scan3 skid storage reference is absent entirely: simh does a bare DownReg(BAR) and drops straight into the third-scan loop, so the byte at (suppression code + 1) is never read or rewritten. (2) The scan1-to-scan2 skid read at (B_high - 1) happens only when the zero-suppress latch is OFF, because C short-circuit evaluation in 'if ((cy & 0x1) == 0 && (ReadP(BAR) & 077) != CHR_0)' skips the ReadP whenever the latch is set - which is precisely the case in which the second scan actually runs. Both are storage-reference and cycle-count deviations only; final register state is unaffected. They matter for cycle-accurate timing and for any storage-protection or address-wrap modelling.

Partial answer to the finder's open question on address wrap during the -1 modification: cube1us models the 1410 scan-modify circuit as wrapping in both directions and raising a latch - T1410CPU::STARScan() sets temp = 0 and StorageWrapLatch = true when the modified address reaches coresize, and temp = 99999 with the same latch when it goes below 0. That is one ALD-derived simulator's reading of the address-modify hardware, not a manual statement; the manual text for MCE says nothing about wrap.

cube1us's scan-2 termination logic is structured differently from S223-2698 p.51 but is behaviourally equivalent on the paths that matter, and it independently confirms the finder's CASE 2 list. It ends the operation at scan 2 when '!FloatingDollarLatch && !DecimalControlLatch' (which covers plain zero suppression, asterisk protection and sign control left - the asterisk-fill latch never forces a third scan, confirming that asterisk protection is a two-scan operation), and it enters scan 3 only when 'FloatingDollarLatch || (ZeroSuppressLatch && !significant_digit)'. Decimal control with a significant digit present therefore also ends at scan 2, because that digit reset the zero-suppress latch during the reverse scan - exactly the finder's CASE 2 row. Verified against A22-0526-3 p.33 Figure 33 example 3 (A-field 00001, control word bbb.bO, result .01 in two scans).
additions.source: https://github.com/cube1us/1410/blob/master/UI1410DATA.cpp (B-cycle subtype 1, scan-2 exit tests); https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf (A22-0526-3, Figure 33 and Decimal Control text, p.33)

additions.claim: A22-0526-3 p.33 contains a wording error in Sign Control Left that should not be encoded: forward scan step 4 reads 'The scan proceeds until the B-field word mark is sensed, indicating the end of the body of the control word.' It is the A-FIELD word mark that ends the body; the B-field word mark ends the first scan. S223-2698 p.50 states it correctly: 'If the A-channel word mark, indicating the end of the A-field, is sensed before the B-channel word mark is detected, the body latch is reset, and the extension latch is set ... The B-channel word mark indicating the end of the B-field terminates the first scan.' The same erroneous sentence is carried into S223-2698's own reprint of the Sign Control Left description on p.49.

The extension latch is set by the skid cycle as well as by the A-field word mark. S223-2698 p.50 (scan1-to-scan2 skid) and p.51 (scan2-to-scan3 skid) both end with 'The extension latch is set during the skid cycle', and cube1us sets next.subscan = SUB_SCAN_E in both skid branches. This matters because the extension subscan is what makes a comma store as a blank in the first scan; after a skid it is simply the resting state for scans 2 and 3.

Register-table row confirmed across all four 1410 PoO printings held on bitsavers, not just the three the finder named: A22-0526 (original), A22-0526-2, A22-0526 May-63 reprint and A22-0526-3 all print 'NSI / A-LA / Varies with result of edit', as do A22-1407-2 Figure 41 p.38 and A22-6726 (7010). The 1410 CE Handbook 223-2588-2 'Brief Op Code Descriptions' Editing row is confirmed to contain no register data and to redirect to 'Reference Manual (Form A24-1407-2)'.

notes:
Method: every 1410 primary source needed was already downloaded and pdftotext-extracted in this project's scratchpad (s2698.txt = S223-2698, princops_a22-0526-3.txt, poo2.txt = A22-0526-2, po.txt = A22-0526 original, po7010.txt = A22-6726, ref1407.txt = A22-1407-2, ceh.txt = 223-2588-2, p1401.txt = A24-1403-5). I re-read the load-bearing passages verbatim rather than trusting the finder's quotes, then fetched cube1us/1410 UI1410DATA.cpp from GitHub for the check the finder explicitly deferred.

Overall verdict: the findings are unusually good. Every 'verified' claim I spot-checked held, verbatim, including all four Figure 34 register values (IAR 00012, AAR 12155, BAR 04677, suppression code at 04676), the S223-2698 -1/+1/-1 narrative, the skid-cycle text at both boundaries, the four scan-termination conditions, the timing formula T = 4.5(L + 1 + A + 1.5B + 1.5Z + 1.5D) with L = 1, 6 or 11, the CE Handbook's 1401-vs-1410 single-character-edit difference, and the 'Varies with result of edit' row across six manuals. I independently re-derived the control-word address layout (04669-04685, 17 characters, '0' at 04676) and it is correct.

The three-scan cases were the real gap, and cube1us closes it. Its third-scan block sets IRingControl and then falls through to Store + Cycle, so the -1 lands on the terminating cycle in all three three-scan paths - CASE 3, 4 and 5 are now confirmed by an ALD-derived implementation as well as by simh and the CE manual's termination wording. I would treat the whole BAR table as safe to implement.

One substantive correction, and it changes emulator output: the finder's fact 19 says no further A-field characters are transferred once the A word mark is sensed. Wrong - the character already in the A-data register is still stored on the FOLLOWING B-cycle (Figure 34 step 36 stores the '0' into 04670 after step 35 sensed the word mark). Only further A-cycles stop. The comma-blanking half of that fact is real but is an extension-subscan rule, not the thing steps 36-37 demonstrate.

One thing I could not settle and will not guess at: whether the 1401's Figure 58 step 33 (no BAR decrement on the first-scan word-mark cycle) is real 1401 behaviour or a print error, since it contradicts the same manual's own 'B-Ln' rule. It does not affect the 1410 answer either way - the 1410 trace is unambiguous - but I flagged it because the two manuals trace the same example with the same control word, which is a live 1401-vs-1410 confusion hazard for anyone reading either figure out of context.

I did not open the 1410 ALDs (bitsavers /pdf/ibm/1410/drawings/); with two independent simulators and the CE narrative agreeing, the marginal value was low. The finder's remaining open questions about per-scan cycle counts in the timing formula and about storage-protection interaction with the skid cycles are still open.
